problem:
The velocity of a particle is $(i-7j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(3i+4j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=3\,\text{h}.$

$v=($
{{field-1}}$i$
$+$
{{field-2}}$j\,)\,\text{km/h}$
worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=i-7j,\,a=3i+4j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=3\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(i-7j)+(3i+4j)(3) \\  & =(i-7j)+(9i+12j) \\  & =(10i+5j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$
